- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or use mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) within last 3–5 days, model overconfidently holds high forecasts — reduce forecast by 2–3% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates downward trends when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0) — adjust downward by 1–2% if sentiment drops below 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 70–75 range — apply a 3–5 day moving average correction if price deviates >3σ from recent 10-day mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 cycles, model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend, especially if sentiment shifts mid-period.
